TRACEABILITY VERDICT: all 57 audit IDs (C1-C8, H1-H13, D1-D4, S1-S4, P1-P7, T1-T3, E1-E5, X1-X5, G1, A1-A6, N1) are covered by at least two findings each, and most by five or more. No ID is completely unmapped. Four are only weakly covered: S3 (cause never reproduced), X2 (cannot be verified from outside), H13 (walkthrough-caption part) and P1 (spike-attribution part). No issue in the audit text is left without a finding. The real gaps are in the plan's structure, not in ID coverage. They are listed under gaps.

METHOD AND CAVEATS: The map below uses each finding's declared refs plus its title. Where I credit a finding for an ID it does not declare (for example mobile-03 for H4), I inferred it from the title. I spot-checked the reports on disk (hist-final-plan.md, app-design.md, pages-A.md) but did not re-read all reports. Verdict tags: UNV = UNVERIFIABLE, NV = NOT_VERIFIED. A finding tagged UNV or NV is not counted as sole coverage for any ID.

gaps.area: Ask the Historian: retrieval architecture, phases, evaluation
gaps.gap: The index has no finding for retrieval architecture (static, hybrid, semantic, optional LLM), for the phased timeline or for governance. Those pieces exist only in files the index omits: hist-final-plan.md (hf-01..hf-37, decision gates G-A1, G-A2, G-X), arch-static-hybrid.md, arch-semantic-local.md, arch-rag-function.md, hist-eval.md and hist-golden-set.json. Read alone, the index looks incomplete for the user's Historian request. Two integration checks are also open. hist-final-plan 10.3 says the floating H1 overlay's interaction with historian.html was not checked. In-app 'Search Units' integration is blocked by N1.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Make hist-final-plan the Historian workstream of record. Fold hist-current-*, hist-sources-1/2-*, data-integrity-27, qa-ci-22, infra-netlify-31, seo-growth-14/23, time-facts-14 and app-time-19 in as inputs to hf-NN items, and add hf-01..hf-37 to the traceability table. Adopt its ten owner decisions with their defaults. Those defaults are records-only positioning, LLM and semantic stages off unless a gate opens, `#q=` fragment deep links, the `/hx/` prefix with the service worker bypassing it, and Git deploys. Add an H1 acceptance test that the overlay does not cover historian.html.

gaps.area: Traceability: new defects with no audit ID
gaps.gap:
The specialists found many critical or high defects the audit never listed. Some have empty refs and some are attached to the wrong ID (the deep-link contract is filed under H3 and H4). The list:
- Dead deep-link contract: 521+ generated links and every 'see it on the map' link land on tick 1 (app-bugs-05, pagesA-03, pages-C-01, pagesB-01, infra-netlify-26, data-integrity-06, ux-flows-01, app-time-06, prov-recon-04, app-latent-12).
- The unit canvas swallows all pointer input, so the map cannot be panned or zoomed (mobile-02, perf-runtime-01, app-latent-04). The audit's 'Works' list contradicts this.
- Turning the sound toggle on crashes playback (app-bugs-03, app-latent-03).
- No error boundary, so any exception blanks the app (app-latent-02, app-bugs-04).
- July 2/3 data is not fetched on a jump (app-bugs-06, app-latent-05).
- Tapping a unit on mobile throws an invalid-LngLat error (app-latent-06).
- Icon-sprite id collision (pagesA-01).
- Mapbox attribution is disabled on two maps, a ToS issue (prov-recon-09, app-design-24, infra-netlify-20, app-latent-27, app-bugs-34).
- Watch Together stored XSS (pages-C-46, app-latent-16, infra-netlify-07).
- The AR iOS permission request loses its user gesture (pages-C-34, app-latent-15).
- Immersive has no hearing-safety limiter (pages-C-26).
- All 137 Historian chronology answers render 'undefined' (hist-current-01, ux-flows-19, pages-C-16, app-latent-13).
- 15 units are on the wrong side and 100 placement ids have no order-of-battle record (app-latent-14, app-bugs-35, data-integrity-02).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Give these their own IDs in the master plan (for example N2-N14). Put the critical ones in Tranche 0 next to C1-C8, and have every section of the final plan cite an ID. Re-baseline the scorecard with them included. The pointer-capture bug goes first: if it is confirmed with real mouse input in a headed browser, it outranks C1.

gaps.area: N1 strategy: rebuild versus bundle patches versus RECON_SRC
gaps.gap:
The index gives competing answers to the missing-source problem.
- prov-recon-01 (Strategy C) is a full TypeScript strangler rebuild, sized XL together with prov-recon-12/14/35-39.
- bundle-anatomy-21 is an AST chunk-splitter stop-gap or source recovery.
- deploy-history-15 is a fidelity diff against a chosen baseline, then porting patches.
- app-bugs-01 (24 string patches), perf-runtime-39, app-a11y-02, docs-copy-32, prov-recon-40 and qa-ci-28 all patch the frozen bundle.
- mobile-21 says RECON_SRC has no mobile layout and cannot host the mobile fixes.
Without one decision, the same fixes will be built twice or the patches will never be retired.
gaps.recommended_plan_item:
Write one architecture decision record.
1. Tranche 0 is a scripted set of patches to the frozen bundle. Each patch asserts its occurrence count, has a Playwright test, and is retired at cutover.
2. In parallel, Phase 0 creates the repository, the parity harness and the strangler rebuild. RECON_SRC is a salvage quarry only.
3. No bundle patch outside the Tranche 0 list is allowed.
The result is that C1, C2, C3, C5, C6, C7 and C8 plus the new critical defects can ship within days while the rebuild proceeds.

gaps.area: Ordering hazard: caching and service worker before any fix
gaps.gap: Assets under /assets are served immutable for a year and the service worker is cache-first. The same asset name has already carried different bytes over time (bundle-anatomy-27, deploy-history-01, mobile-19, app-time-13), and the service worker caches 404 and 500 responses (app-latent-11). Any bundle or data fix can therefore be invisible to returning visitors or can poison caches unless the service-worker kill-switch and content-hashed names ship first. Two further hazards: the Netlify-downloaded zip has lower-cased asset names (bundle-anatomy-05), so redeploying it would 404 the app, and each production deploy costs Netlify credits on credit plans (infra-netlify-30; hist-final-plan 1.4 says 15 credits, plan unverified).
gaps.recommended_plan_item:
Make this a hard dependency chain in the master plan.
0. Archive all zips and use the correct-case tree.
1. Deploy the self-unregistering service-worker kill-switch, remove the controllerchange reload, and switch to content-hashed filenames.
2. Ship everything else.
Add a first-visit and returning-visit Playwright test (qa-ci-08) proving that the new bytes reach both. Batch deploys and confirm the Netlify plan and credit balance first.

gaps.area: Master schedule and solo-maintainer capacity
gaps.gap: By my count the index has about 27 non-refuted findings rated XL, plus many L. The Historian core alone is estimated at 49-76 person-days, or 26-40 calendar weeks at 15 h/week (hist-final-plan 0.1). prov-recon-41 rolls up only the rebuild effort, and no finding merges the whole plan into one critical path. Without that, 'A+ in every category' has no achievable order, no stop rules and no minimum path.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add one integrated roadmap. It should include a dependency graph across workstreams, a WIP limit, and grade-impact-per-day ordering. It should distinguish the minimum path to A from the full path to A+, and set per-category exit criteria using the qa-ci-23 scorecard. Stop rules, such as hist-final-plan's decision gates, should apply to every optional workstream.

gaps.area: Conflicting design decisions that need ADRs before any build
gaps.gap:
The specialists disagree on several architecture choices.
- Map engine: bundle-anatomy-16 (a spike comparing Mapbox v3 lazy, v2.15, MapLibre, Leaflet-lite and own tiles) versus prov-recon-10/19 (pin and lazy-load 3.24.1).
- Unit rendering: perf-runtime-17 (make the canvas cheap) versus perf-runtime-10, app-design-21 and mobile-24 (Mapbox symbol layers).
- Site generator: prov-recon-35 (Astro) versus pagesA-39 (a manifest-driven shared build).
- Home page: seo-growth-09 (landing-first, app moves to /map) versus the URL, PWA and deep-link stability that prov-recon-36 and ux-flows-01 protect.
- Shell: one responsive shell (app-design-02, prov-recon-14) versus mobile-22's separate mobile component system.
- Telemetry: perf-cwv-17, qa-ci-16, ux-flows-21, seo-growth-35, bundle-anatomy-06, infra-netlify-32 and app-latent-36 each specify their own pipeline.
- CSP: infra-netlify-01, deploy-history-18 and qa-ci-13 use different staging.
- Source maps (P6): public or private, unresolved.
- Sound policy: prov-recon-29.
- Historian AI posture: hist-final-plan decision 2 versus infra-netlify-31.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Write an ADR for each decision, each with a stated default and a spike where needed. Order them so the map-engine and unit-rendering spikes and the landing-versus-map URL decision come first, because they gate the boot, performance and SEO work. Merge the telemetry proposals into one privacy-reviewed collector. Decide the source-map policy alongside CSP.

gaps.area: Audit statements contradicted by the specialists (re-baseline)
gaps.gap:
Several audit statements or BRIEF premises do not survive.
- X1: the audit says the Mapbox token returned 200 for a foreign Referer. mobile-20 and pagesA-38 found tile requests return 403 for foreign and localhost Referers.
- X4: the audit called user-guide.pdf inline, but it is an attachment (already corrected in the BRIEF).
- H3: the audit says a ~15 s splash. bundle-anatomy-13 and perf-cwv-04 measured the intro itself at 3.5 s. The 15 s is not reproduced in the index and may be the whole first-run sequence.
- 'Works' claims contradicted: the Follow-Ancestor share link white-screens (app-latent-01), pan and zoom are swallowed (perf-runtime-01), mobile tap-select throws (app-latent-06), and sound-on crashes (app-bugs-03).
- D3: the empty July 3 fields are a data-loading bug, not only a camera issue (app-bugs-06).
- 'CLS mostly fixed' versus deploy-history-25 and perf-cwv-15.
- 'Sub-pages strong or good on mobile' versus pagesA-10/26 (Dashboard widens the phone layout to 446 px, Compare to 528 px) and pagesB-14 (documentary renders as one paragraph).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add an audit-corrections annex to the plan. It records the corrected X1, X4 and H3 wording, and re-scores the scorecard from the specialists' evidence. Treat X1 as 'verify first' (see the keys gap).

gaps.area: S3: Camera and Viewshed canvas painted incompletely
gaps.gap: S3 is only weakly covered. pagesA-34 says it could not be reproduced and calls it 'hardened, not fixed'. pagesB-41 and pages-C-* only cover adjacent resize and layout-shift issues. The named suspect is `#atmosphere{mix-blend-mode:multiply}` at camera.html:38, and the cause is unconfirmed.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add S3 to the real-device programme (qa-ci-21) and run it on a GPU-backed headed browser. Add a paint gate to the Playwright suite: wait for the map's idle event, call resize() after layout changes, and assert the canvas is non-blank. Test the atmosphere overlay with mix-blend-mode removed. If the artifact cannot be reproduced on real hardware, close S3 with that evidence and keep the gate.

gaps.area: X1 and X2: API keys need owner action
gaps.gap: The Mapbox token's real restriction state is disputed between the audit (unrestricted) and mobile-20 and pagesA-38 (URL-restricted for tiles). Restrictions may also differ per API family (tiles versus styles, fonts, geocoding). The Google Maps embed key (X2) cannot be judged from outside. mobile-20 also notes the URL restriction makes local development impossible, so a separate dev token is needed. None of this can be verified or fixed by code.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a Phase-0 owner checklist. In the Mapbox account, review the token's URL restrictions and scopes and create a separate dev or preview token. In Google Cloud, restrict the key by HTTP referrer and to the Maps Embed API only, or remove it with click-to-load and a keyless link. Add billing alerts. Add secret scanning before the first commit (prov-recon-08). Record the results, then keep X1 and X2 as CI contract tests (qa-ci-13).

gaps.area: Verification debt and the audit's untested areas
gaps.gap: The audit lists what it did not test: real touch on a phone, Safari and Firefox, screen readers, audio, Cinematic Export recording, Watch Together live sync, AR on site, and Street View inside the walkthrough. By my count the index carries about 25 UNVERIFIABLE and 18 NOT_VERIFIED findings, plus 1 REFUTED (time-facts-15). Several touch audit IDs: deploy-history-31 and deploy-history-33 (H13, P1), pagesB-16 and pagesB-32 (S4), app-a11y-20 (C1, C2), perf-runtime-36 (P7), pages-C-40 (H7) and pages-C-84 (X5). Most of the Immersive, AR, Cinematic Export, Watch Together, Turning Points and Living Ledger findings (pages-C-21..43, 61-62, 67, 73-74, 79-80) are NV.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Create a verification-debt register. Before any UNV or NV item is scheduled, do a time-boxed verification: real phone, iOS Safari, Firefox, NVDA or VoiceOver, an audio check, a two-browser Watch Together session, an on-site AR trial and an export recording test. Drop refuted items such as time-facts-15. Wire the register to qa-ci-21 and app-a11y-33 (the manual assistive-technology programme).

gaps.area: Definition of 'green' and the map-page performance ceiling
gaps.gap: Netlify RUM p75 aggregates every page view, including the 9 sub-pages that block first paint on a 1.8 MB CDN Mapbox script (FCP 3.3-5.5 s per pagesA-28, pagesB-02, perf-runtime-11) and the map app. Netlify RUM is a 30-day rolling window (per the RUM PDF the audit used), so it turns green about a month after the fixes. No finding states the fallback if a full-viewport Mapbox map cannot reach Lighthouse mobile 95+ under throttling. The pieces exist (bundle-anatomy-16, perf-cwv-26, ux-flows-15, seo-growth-09) but there is no explicit go or no-go criterion.
gaps.recommended_plan_item:
Add a performance-target section that does four things.
1. Give the map route and each sub-page template their own budgets.
2. Use first-party per-route RUM for fast feedback (perf-cwv-17) and the Netlify 30-day p75 for the official green, and tell the owner to expect roughly a month of lag.
3. Ship the cheap wins first (C6 reload, body fade-in, boot-after-first-paint, deferring the Mapbox script on sub-pages) so the window starts clearing early.
4. Set a fallback: if the map spike misses, make the static landing or text route the Lighthouse target and keep the map as an opt-in second stage.

gaps.area: Human historical review as a blocking dependency
gaps.gap: The historical A+ (C4, H10, data consistency graded C-) cannot be reached by engineering alone. The index carries a review queue of 5 review anchors, 33 disagreements and 45 low-confidence rows (time-facts-05), a verification backlog (data-integrity-29), and hist-final-plan decision 3 ('name a historical reviewer before P4'). Nothing schedules this reviewer or defines what ships before sign-off.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Name a reviewer, for example a licensed battlefield guide or a Gettysburg historical society or NPS contact, before C4 data changes go live. Schedule 3-4 reviewer hours per week. Until sign-off, ship the corrected model with visible 'approximate time' markers (time-facts-13) and a public corrections page (docs-copy-18). Make the reviewer's sign-off the exit criterion for the 'Historical consistency' category.

gaps.area: Privacy and legal work must precede new telemetry and functions
gaps.gap: Several findings add new data flows or third-party calls: a first-party web-vitals beacon (perf-cwv-17), analytics and events (seo-growth-35, ux-flows-21), the RUM and CSP collector (infra-netlify-10), an optional LLM function (infra-netlify-31, hist-final-plan C-lite) and a Watch Together relay (pages-C-47). The current privacy page is inaccurate or incomplete (X5: pages-C-81, deploy-history-17), and some of these features would contradict it.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Gate all new telemetry, analytics, functions and relay work on the X5 privacy and Terms rewrite (infra-netlify-36/37) and the consent-posture decision (infra-netlify-38). Update the CSP connect-src list in the same release as any new endpoint.

gaps.area: Rights retro-audit of already-shipped data
gaps.gap:
Some rights exposure is already live and carries no audit ID.
- hist-sources-1-04 says the order-of-battle provenance leans on copyrighted compilations.
- hist-final-plan risk 1 says 18 shipped monument coordinates derive from Stone Sentinels (8), HMDB (4) and Wikipedia (6).

The plan schedules the source registry and tier gate for the new corpus (hist-sources-1-11, hist-sources-2-01/18/20, hist-final-plan hf-01), but nothing puts the audit of existing data ahead of ingesting new sources.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Make the retro-audit of shipped data the first task of the source-registry phase. Tag existing rows as legacy with a source and rights tier. Replace or attribute the flagged rows. Get counsel to review the Busey and Martin-derived figures. Add the CI tier gate before Wave 2 ingestion starts.

summary: Read BRIEF.md, the finding index, and grepped/read the specialist reports (prov-recon, perf-cwv, ux-flows, seo-growth, infra-netlify, qa-ci, hist-final-plan, bundle-anatomy, pages-C, app-mobile) plus deploy/index.html, deploy/privacy.html and bundle.pretty.js:112960-112996 to verify each claim. The specialists cover most technical categories in depth (print, light/dark theming, offline/SW, Mapbox attribution and billing, monitoring, CI minutes, real-device QA, Historian rights/eval). What still blocks an honest A+ falls into three groups. (1) Programme-level, most severe: the summed effort exceeds one solo owner's capacity by years; specialist reports contradict each other on canonical URL form, what '/' is, and whether an entry gate exists (which the 95+ mobile score depends on); the 94-100 mobile projections exclude real Mapbox tile/GL cost. (2) Platform gaps nobody owns: browser support floor, WebGL context loss, browser auto-translate/forced-dark/blockers, non-QWERTY keyboards, school-network reachability, in-app browsers, long sessions. (3) Governance gaps: no backup/DR/continuity, no ops-load ceiling, no counsel review, no named site-wide historical reviewer, no independent verification, no citation permanence, no vendor exit triggers, single Gmail contact conflicting with proposed null-MX DNS, and SEO changes that would overlap with no baseline. Twenty concrete items follow. Not verified: exact costs of external audits/attorney review, per-vendor school-filter behaviour, iOS canvas-memory limits, whether Mapbox supports a hard spend cap.

gaps.area: Programme / capacity (all categories)
gaps.gap: No report reconciles total effort with one solo owner. Stated roll-ups: prov-recon-41 38-50 AI-assisted days (65 unassisted) at prov-recon.md:995; hist-final-plan 49-76 days core, which it itself converts to 26-40 calendar weeks at 15 h/week (hist-final-plan.md:23); seo-growth 77.5 days (seo-growth.md:716); app-a11y about 50 (app-a11y.md:1103); infra-netlify 35-45 (infra-netlify.md:1695); docs-copy 42-45 (docs-copy.md:1487,1580); pages-C 95-100 (pages-C.md:937). Gross sum of just these seven is about 385-445 person-days before de-duplication (many findings carry 'Overlaps:' lines). At 15 h/week (about 1.9 d/week, my arithmetic) that is 200+ weeks; even after a 40% overlap haircut it is about 2.4-2.7 years. Several XL items (renderer migration, on-site/AR mode, WebCodecs export, programmatic SEO engine, real viewshed) each exceed a month. Without a scope contract the likely outcome is two half-finished apps and no A+ anywhere.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Programme scope and capacity' (S-M, 2 days). (1) Build one de-duplicated WBS: merge overlaps (dialog/token/shell work across a11y, design and prov-recon; time model across 4 reports; deep links across 9; service worker across 6) and re-total. (2) Define A+ scope tiers: Tier 1 must reach A+ on desktop and mobile = landing '/', /map app, Search, Historian, Dashboard, Report/Regiment, legal pages, 404/embed; Tier 2 = other content pages; Tier 3 'Labs' = AR, Watch Together, Cinematic Export, Sandbox, 'What They Could See', unit-rendering-reference, Sound. Each Labs feature gets a dated ship-or-retire decision (retire = 301 to a parent page or 410, removed from nav, sitemap, guide and code) because an A+ grade allows no known defects and a 'beta' badge does not fix them. (3) WIP limit of 2 workstreams and stop rules per phase (reuse prov-recon-41's 20% slip rule and hist-final-plan 9.4). (4) Record available hours/week and publish a Tier-1-only 'A+ by date X' milestone on the scorecard (qa-ci-23). Acceptance: de-duplicated effort is at most hours available times weeks to target date with 30% contingency; every Tier 3 feature has a disposition row.

gaps.area: Programme / decision register (contradictions between reports)
gaps.gap: Specialists give incompatible answers that block sequencing and CI gates. (a) Canonical URL: prov-recon-35 keeps '.html' canonicals with build.format 'file' (prov-recon.md:440,1063); infra-netlify-11 (infra-netlify.md:277) and seo-growth-03 (seo-growth.md:117) choose extensionless; qa-ci still lists it as an open question (qa-ci.md:1535). (b) What '/' is: seo-growth-09 makes '/' a static landing and moves the app to '/map' (noindex,follow); ux-flows.md:500 and prov-recon-16 keep the map at '/'. (c) Entry gate: perf-cwv option D (97-100) is legitimate only because 'the user must decide anyway' at the chooser (perf-cwv.md:496), while ux-flows-02, app-design-14 and prov-recon-28 delete the chooser. (d) Service worker: hand-rolled (prov-recon-17) vs Workbox (infra-netlify-22). Also pending owner choices: product name, keep/remove sound (prov-recon Q1), day-tab anchor (app-time section 13), Strategy C go/no-go, map engine (bundle-anatomy-16), contact mailbox vs DNS records.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a Decision Register as a Phase-0 exit criterion (S, 1 day), one ADR per row with a default and a decide-by phase. Recommended defaults: D1 extensionless clean URLs, decided now because at about 175 search referrals per 30 days the reconsolidation cost is lowest today (overrides prov-recon-35's file format; CI gates SL-16/HP-10 and the sitemap generator read this value). D2 static landing at '/', app at '/map', PWA start_url '/map', and an inline script forwards legacy '/?ancestor=&tick=...' to '/map' when app params exist. D3 no chooser; boot contract from the perf spike (next item). D4 one custom versioned SW (prov-recon-17, kill-switch first); Workbox only if the offline pack ships. D5 name, sound, day tabs, Strategy C, map engine, contact addresses. Acceptance: register file signed off by the owner; no report item remains 'depends on owner decision' without a linked ADR.

gaps.area: Performance (LCP/INP/TBT, Lighthouse 95+ mobile, RUM green)
gaps.gap: The mobile 94-100 projections are upper bounds: perf-cwv's own verification says replica runs exclude Mapbox tile/GL work because api.mapbox.com returns 403 off-production (perf-cwv.md:857, and LHCI on previews measures a different workload, same list item 4). Once the chooser is deleted (see decision register) nothing user-driven gates the map boot, and ux-flows-02 autoplays a roughly 20 s guided moment (ticks 535-556) on first run. perf-cwv.md:496 warns it is 'not legitimate to delay the app merely to dodge the trace'. Separately, RUM volume is about 113 views/day (seo-growth.md:70) and about 1,600 non-home views per 30 days across 26 pages (BRIEF), so per-page p75 cannot reach the n>=200 threshold qa-ci uses.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a 2-day 'boot-contract spike' before budgets are locked. (a) Reproduce production-equivalent load: CDP Fetch interception injecting Referer https://gettysburginteractivemap.com/ for api.mapbox.com (or an allow-listed CI token on preview hosts); measure /map on Moto G Power-class and ChromeOS profiles with a real map init. (b) Choose the contract: '/' static landing with no map JS; '/map' shows a poster-with-CTA facade for first-time visitors and boots on tap or after idle of at least 3 s, while returning/deep-link visitors boot immediately; the guided moment starts only after a user gesture (also fixes autoplay/reduced-motion). (c) Publish which URLs are Lighthouse-scored for the A+ claim, including '/map'; if measured '/map' mobile stays under 95 after all fixes, record the measured ceiling as a documented exception rather than hiding the boot from the trace. (d) Accept RUM per template (landing, /map desktop, /map mobile, content pages, tool pages), not per URL, using the first-party humans-only beacon (perf-cwv-17). Acceptance: budgets.json numbers come from runs with real tiles; CI uses the same interception.

gaps.area: Cross-browser / support policy (iOS Safari, Samsung Internet, older WebViews)
gaps.gap: No report defines a browser support floor: a grep of all specialist reports finds zero hits for 'browserslist', 'iOS 15' or 'Safari 15'. bundle-anatomy-19 hard-codes build.target 'es2022' (bundle-anatomy.md:375) although its own verifier measured only about 0.3-0.6 KB br gain (bundle-anatomy.md:772). Mapbox GL v3 requires WebGL2 (prov-recon-10), which drops older iOS/Android WebViews. The plans add CSS/APIs with differing support (cascade layers, dvh, container queries, :has, inert, color-mix, Speculation Rules Chromium-only, OffscreenCanvas, WebGPU/ORT-Web in arch-semantic-local). A syntax-level failure on an older Safari yields a blank white page, and the current app has no ErrorBoundary to show anything (app-latent-02).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Browser support policy' (S). Write docs/BROWSERS.md and a package.json browserslist from real UA share (Netlify Analytics/RUM UA breakdown). Default proposal: last 2 majors of Chrome/Edge/Firefox, Safari and iOS 16+ (confirm against share), Samsung Internet last 2, ChromeOS current LTS. Derive build.target and CSS targets (lightningcss) from it instead of hard-coding es2022. Add an es-check gate on dist/*.js and a caniuse-lite CSS/API audit to CI. Feature-detect module support and WebGL2 and route failing clients to the Text/Chronicle route (ux-flows-15) with an inline message so failure is visible, not blank. Add one physical iPhone SE (2nd gen) and one Samsung Internet device per release candidate (qa-ci T6). Acceptance: dist passes es-check at the policy level; forcing WebGL2 off shows the fallback; policy linked from Help.

gaps.area: Reliability / mobile GPU and memory (WebGL context loss)
gaps.gap: app-mobile.md:945 confirms the app has no webglcontextlost handling; qa-ci.md:647 lists context loss only as a Safari risk to eyeball. No finding converts it into a fix. iOS Safari and low-RAM Android reclaim GPU contexts on backgrounding or memory pressure, and today up to 3 Mapbox instances plus a full-viewport unit canvas without DPR can coexist (app-mobile.md:267). The planned DPR-aware canvases (app-design-20) increase backing-store size, and iOS Safari limits canvas area and total canvas memory (exact limits unverified). After a loss the map stays black with no error UI.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'GPU resilience' (M). (1) Listen for map webglcontextlost/webglcontextrestored (Mapbox emits both; verify on 3.24.1) and the same events on any owned canvas: pause rAF, show a StateCard ('Map paused, resuming'), re-add sources/layers from one idempotent addLayers(map), and after 3 losses in 60 s fall back to the Text/Chronicle route. (2) Assert one WebGL context per page (qa-ci-11) and cap owned canvases at min(dpr,2) and about 8 M px on iOS, lower under Save-Data. (3) visibilitychange/pagehide: pause playback and audio; never create a second map on bfcache restore. (4) Adaptive quality by measured frame time (Safari lacks deviceMemory): drop labels/trails/DPR when p95 frame time exceeds 34 ms for 3 s. Acceptance: Playwright calls WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext()/restoreContext() and recovery takes under 3 s across 20 cycles with zero uncaught errors; manual iPhone SE background/foreground x10.

gaps.area: Cross-browser / i18n (browser-injected transformations)
gaps.gap: deploy/index.html has lang='en' but no translate='no' (also confirmed in app-latent.md:43) and no color-scheme meta (head contains only viewport and theme-color). About 18% of views come from DE/CN/SG/HK (BRIEF T2; the human share is unknown), and real international visitors commonly use Chrome/Edge auto-translate, which rewrites text nodes and is a well-known trigger of React 'removeChild' crashes in apps with dynamic text (general knowledge, not reproduced here). Samsung Internet and Chrome forced-dark or Dark Reader invert the satellite canvas and gold-on-dark palette; app-design-28 handles only prefers-color-scheme. Content blockers (Brave, uBlock) block events.mapbox.com and the RUM script, producing ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT console errors that conflict with the zero-console-errors bar. No report states a language scope; the Spanish-classroom question is open at ux-flows.md:1881.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Hostile-environment hardening' (S-M). (a) Record an English-only stance in the decision register; put translate='no' on the map stage, canvas labels, unit names and clocks (and notranslate meta on /map only; content pages stay translatable); the ErrorBoundary treats DOM-mutation errors with a Reload prompt. (b) Add a color-scheme meta and CSS per theme and a forced-dark test using --enable-features=WebContentsForceDark. (c) Make telemetry failure silent: Mapbox performanceMetricsCollection off, wrapped beacons, never surface errors from blocked third-party requests; define 'zero console errors' as measured in a clean profile AND with uBlock Origin default lists (Playwright extension context). (d) Add Chrome auto-translate (es/de) to the QA matrix for the 3 main flows. Acceptance: app stays usable with translation on; the blocker run shows 0 console errors.

gaps.area: Accessibility / usability (keyboard layouts, IME)
gaps.gap: The global key handler switches on Ur.key with case '1','2','3' for day jumps and ignores only tagName INPUT (bundle.pretty.js:112966-112993). On French/Belgian AZERTY the unshifted digit row produces '&', 'é', '"', so the day-jump keys never fire (numpad still works); single-key letter shortcuts (S, F, L, B, ?) behave differently on Dvorak/Colemak/QWERTZ; IME composition can trigger shortcuts. Neither prov-recon-31 nor app-a11y-06 (the planned hotkey registry) specifies layout independence, and a grep of all reports finds no AZERTY, event.code or isComposing.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Extend the single hotkey registry (S): each binding declares `code` (positional: Digit1-3/Numpad1-3, Arrow*, Space) or `key` (mnemonic), matched code-first then key; ignore events with isComposing or targets input/textarea/select/[contenteditable]/[role=textbox]; keep the WCAG 2.1.4 toggle to disable single-key shortcuts; generate Help from the registry with layout-neutral labels ('1 to 3', not key glyphs). Route every clock/number/date string through one Intl formatter with explicit 'en-US' so device locale never changes output (the bundle has 13 toLocaleString/Intl call sites). Acceptance: Playwright dispatches KeyboardEvent {key:'&', code:'Digit1'} and jumps to Day 1; typing in an IME composition triggers nothing.

gaps.area: Usability / schools and classrooms (reachability, low-end Chromebooks, sensitive content)
gaps.gap: ux-flows personas put about 60% of student traffic on managed Chromebooks (ux-flows.md:76) with 30 students loading at once (ux-flows.md:260); the domain was registered 2026-06-13 (infra-netlify.md:58). A grep of all reports finds nothing on school web-filter categorisation (GoGuardian, Securly, Lightspeed, Cisco Umbrella, Fortinet, Palo Alto), on the exact domains a classroom must allow (api.mapbox.com, events.mapbox.com, ingesteer.services-prod.nsvcs.net, Google Maps embed, 0.peerjs.com plus STUN/TURN), or on a ChromeOS low-end profile as a performance target. Filters commonly default-block uncategorised sites and WebRTC (per-vendor behaviour unverified). hist-final-plan.md:852 defaults to quoting period racial language faithfully with an optional hide, which is not a safe default for under-18 Classroom mode.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'School readiness' (M). (1) After landing and teach pages are stable, submit the domain to the major filter vendors' public categorisation forms (Education/Reference/History) and log dates. (2) Publish /teach/it-admin (extending seo-growth-31) listing exact domains/ports per feature, and define a Classroom mode that needs only the site plus api.mapbox.com and disables WebRTC, Street View and YouTube by default (ux-flows-13). (3) Add a ChromeOS profile (4 GB, Celeron-class, 4x CPU, Slow 4G, 30 concurrent sessions) to qa-ci perf profiles and test one real Chromebook per release candidate. (4) In Classroom/Student mode, collapse passages flagged sensitive (period racial language, atrocity accounts) behind a content note by default with a teacher toggle; Historian, Documentary and vignettes honour it. Acceptance: classroom-mode e2e passes with third-party hosts blocked; IT-admin list verified against a network capture.

gaps.area: Reliability / backups, disaster recovery, bus factor
gaps.gap: No report contains a backup, restore or disaster-recovery item (grep hits are unrelated scanner rules; only prov-recon-02's one-time zip archive and the Historian raw-source cache exist). Single points of failure are evidenced: one Gmail address is the public contact everywhere (privacy.html, terms.html, site-nav.js) and the CAA iodef target (infra-netlify.md:634), and infra-netlify.md:669 hedges on separating it from the recovery mailbox 'if possible'; the registrar term ends 2027-06-13 with multi-year renewal only a recommendation (infra-netlify.md:58); Search Console ownership already lapsed (seo-growth-01); deploy history exists only as zips on one PC; the pipeline's raw-source/OCR cache (75 MB+; hist-final-plan.md:746) is outside git; RUM data will live in Netlify Blobs.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Backup, restore and continuity' (M). (1) 3-2-1: private GitHub repo plus a second remote (GitLab or bare repo on external disk) plus a monthly encrypted release bundle to cloud storage; large/raw artifacts (raw-source cache, OCR, golden sets) via git-lfs or a hashed archive with manifest. (2) A secret-free /ops/inventory.yaml: Netlify settings, env var NAMES, DNS zone export, registrar, Mapbox token URL restrictions and scopes, Google key restrictions, GSC/Bing owners, alert routes; secrets in a password manager with emergency access for a named delegate. (3) Quarterly restore drill: from an empty machine, rebuild and deploy to a fresh Netlify site in 2 h or less, logged. (4) A static 'lite' snapshot (landing, Text/Chronicle, legal) deployable to a second host with a documented DNS switch, RTO 4 h or less. (5) A continuity letter: who holds access, how to keep domain and renewals alive, and a sunset plan (freeze to a static archive with a 'not updated since' banner). Acceptance: drill log dated within 90 days; delegate can renew the domain; repo restores from the second remote.

gaps.area: Maintenance / operations load for a solo owner
gaps.gap: Recurring duties are specified in separate reports and never summed: Historian review 3-4 h/week plus corrections acknowledged within 3 days (hist-final-plan.md:421-425), weekly/monthly SEO routines (seo-growth-37), bot segmentation (seo-growth-36), RUM/error triage (qa-ci-16/17), dependency PRs (infra-netlify-39), manual AT/real-device runs per release (qa-ci T6), user-research loops (ux-flows-22), editorial calendar and outreach (seo-growth-30/34). No report defines a steady-state ceiling, a dependency-currency policy (mapbox-gl 3.x cadence, React/zustand pins, Node LTS, Astro) or a maintenance mode. Because much of the build is planned as Claude-assisted, if the owner cannot review or run the code unaided the bus factor is the tooling, not the person (docs-copy.md:1324 mentions bus factor only for documentation).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Sustainable operations' (S-M). (1) Recurring-duties table: hours/month, automation level, alert threshold; cap steady-state human load (proposal: 10 h/month excluding content work) and automate the rest with alerts. (2) Define maintenance mode: which duties pause (outreach, new content) versus never (security patches, certificate/domain renewals, corrections). (3) Dependency-currency ADR: Renovate patch auto-merge only when CI is green; mapbox-gl minors quarterly behind the parity harness; majors yearly; Node LTS in .nvmrc. (4) Maintainability contract for AI-assisted code: direct-dependency budget enforced in CI, one ADR per non-obvious choice, every runbook executable by the owner in 30 min without an AI session, tests as the safety net, commit trailers recording assistance. (5) 30-minute monthly ops review checklist. Acceptance: table exists, all alerts route to one channel, each runbook dry-run by the owner is logged.

gaps.area: Legal / privacy / rights (COPPA, GDPR, minors, UGC, LLM tier)
gaps.gap: Five reports independently draft or rewrite Privacy/Terms (infra-netlify-36/37 with full drafts from infra-netlify.md:1531, docs-copy-25, pages-C-81/83/84, deploy-history-17) with no single owner and no professional review; pages-C.md:957 says legal points 'need professional review'; arch-rag-function.md:959 says AI-disclosure and provider minor-audience obligations 'were not verified'; hist reports defer to counsel on public-domain arithmetic, Busey and Martin-derived figures and embeddings-as-adaptation (arch-semantic-local.md:1016). The infra draft says no data from children under 13 (COPPA) or under 16 (GDPR) (infra-netlify.md:1531), a simplification (GDPR Art. 8 lets member states choose 13-16), and claims 'collects no personal information' despite Netlify logs/IPs, PeerJS IP exposure and a Gmail feedback channel. Watch Together shares user-written text between peers on a site aimed at minors.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Legal and rights pack' (M plus a one-time attorney review; cost unverified). (1) A data-flow inventory (Netlify logs/RUM, Mapbox telemetry, Google embeds, PeerJS/STUN, optional LLM, Name.com, GitHub) feeding ONE Privacy Policy and Terms merged from the five drafts, versioned with a change log. (2) Counsel-checked age wording, a classroom/student statement (no accounts, no PII, third parties off in Classroom mode) and an ePrivacy analysis of localStorage/SW cache. (3) UGC policy: retire free-text peer sharing or add limits plus a report path; decide a DMCA agent only if UGC remains. (4) Trademark/branding review: non-affiliation notice for NPS/Gettysburg Foundation and the naming-confusion risk with the paid 'Gettysburg Animated Battle Map' app (seo-growth R12). (5) One content and data licence (seo-growth-26/infra-37) matched to /sources. (6) Gate any LLM tier on written confirmation that the provider's usage policy permits a product used by minors. (7) Accessibility legal posture (ADA/508 buyers expect an ACR). Acceptance: counsel sign-off recorded; every Privacy claim is covered by the network-log CI test (hist-final-plan risk 16).

gaps.area: Rights / derived media (imagery, video, OG, print)
gaps.gap: Derived media from Mapbox imagery are planned with no rights decision. seo-growth.md:105 builds the default OG card from 'a crop of a real map screenshot' (deferring to seo-growth-11 for attribution) while seo-growth.md:304 says OG art has 'no third-party basemap imagery'; seo-growth-33 plans a YouTube channel from Cinematic Export; docs-copy plans guide and press-kit screenshots; pages-C.md:39 and :1023 record that Mapbox attribution guidance covers live and static maps but video 'is not addressed', and pages-C.md:957 flags legal review. Satellite imagery is also third-party content (provider credits to verify).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Decide one media policy in the decision register and the media-rights register (hist-sources-2-20) (S-M). Default option 1: all derived/republished media (OG cards, SVG mini-maps, exported video, print/PDF, press kit, embed thumbnails, YouTube) render on a public-domain basemap we control (USGS 3DEP hillshade/NAIP-derived tiles or pure vector SVG from placements and terrain; see bundle-anatomy option F and seo-growth-12), reserving Mapbox imagery for the live interactive map. Option 2: obtain written confirmation from Mapbox support for screenshot/video reuse with logo and text attribution burned in (pages-C-69) and store it in the register. Add a CI check that every shipped raster/video asset has a register row with source and licence. Acceptance: register covers 100% of shipped raster assets; under option 2 every exported video/PDF shows attribution.

gaps.area: Security / contact identity and support channel
gaps.gap: The only contact is one personal-looking Gmail (mailto in privacy.html, terms.html and site-nav.js, verified in deploy/), reused as the CAA iodef target and likely the account-recovery identity (infra-netlify.md:634,669). infra-netlify-34 proposes null MX, SPF '-all' and DMARC reject (infra-netlify.md:626-640), which would make any role address on the domain impossible, contradicting the planned intake channels: corrections and Report-a-problem (docs-copy-18, ux-flows section 8.3), security.txt, permission emails (hist-final-plan decision 7), takedown/DMCA, teacher outreach. hist-final-plan.md:425 promises acknowledgement within 3 days, but no triage owner, spam handling or SLA exists, and pagesA-08 flags the harvestable mailto.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Contact architecture' (S). Choose in the decision register: role addresses on the domain (contact@, security@, corrections@) via free email routing/forwarding or a Workspace alias, and then publish the forwarder's MX/SPF/DKIM plus DMARC INSTEAD of infra-netlify-34's null-MX/-all rows (amend that item). Keep the account-recovery mailbox private and separate, with passkeys/2FA. Replace shipped mailto text with a Report-a-problem form (Netlify Forms or a function; update the privacy page) plus an obfuscated mailto fallback. Add an auto-responder, triage labels, a 3-day ack SLA and a spam filter; point security.txt Contact at security@. Acceptance: test mail to every alias arrives; DMARC alignment passes for forwarded mail; a grep test finds no personal Gmail in shipped HTML.

gaps.area: Data accuracy / historical-accuracy governance (site-wide and Ask the Historian)
gaps.gap: hist-final-plan.md:32 makes a 'named historical reviewer' a P4 prerequisite for the Historian corpus only and says P4 stalls without one (hist-final-plan.md:809). Site-wide data has the same dependency with no owner: time-facts-05 (5 review anchors, 33 source disagreements, 45 low-confidence rows), data-integrity-29's verification backlog, docs-copy-33's headline statistics and quotations, pages-B-25's fact-check list, and prov-recon.md:1062 ('anchor table signed off by a historian'). No item says how to find, engage or credit that person, what happens if nobody is found, or how unreviewed content is labelled. A+ data accuracy cannot be self-certified by the owner or by the AI toolchain that produced the data.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Historical review board and editorial standard' (S to set up, then 3-4 h/week). (1) Recruit one named reviewer and one second reader (licensed battlefield guides, a Civil War Round Table, park-adjacent historians, a university); the permission outreach in hist-final-plan decision 7 can carry the ask. One-page charter: scope, hours, credit line on /sources and /corrections, decision-log format (committed decisions.jsonl), right to veto a claim. (2) Editorial standard: evidence classes documented/reconstructed/schematic (data-integrity basis field), contested-fact rule (show range plus sources), quotation and responsible-language policy (docs-copy-27), 1863 clock wording. (3) Release stamps: the data manifest records reviewed_by/at per dataset; unreviewed items show an 'Unreviewed reconstruction' badge; nothing may say 'Reviewed' without a signed decision. (4) Fallback: if no reviewer is found by the deadline, ship with the visible unreviewed labelling and capped claims (no 'accurate to the minute') instead of blocking. (5) Quarterly review of corrections and the 100-answer Historian audit. Acceptance: charter and named reviewer published; reviewed-coverage percentage shown per dataset; CI fails if copy says 'Reviewed' without a matching decision record.

gaps.area: Verification / independent evidence for A+ claims
gaps.gap: Every grade comes from the owner-plus-AI toolchain: the accessibility conformance report is self-written (app-a11y-34), the Historian golden set is single-author (hist-final-plan risk 12), the usability programme is marked UNVERIFIABLE with no recruiting path (ux-flows-22), design consistency is judged by tokens and lint (app-design-34), and security by self-run header scans. An honest public A+ claim needs at least some third-party evidence, and none of the 30 reports plans it.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add an 'A+ acceptance dossier' (M; external costs unverified, owner sets budget). Before claiming A+ publicly collect: (a) an independent accessibility evaluation of 6 key flows by a third party or a volunteer group with disabled testers (screen reader, voice/switch, low vision), published in the accessibility statement, keeping 'partially conforms' wording until then; (b) WebPageTest or real-device runs on a physical mid-range Android and an iPhone SE for all Tier-1 URLs, archived; (c) MDN Observatory and securityheaders scans plus an outside peer review of CSP/headers; (d) a one-hour professional design/UX critique of /map (mobile and desktop), landing and Historian; (e) 8-10 real-user sessions across the three personas (ux-flows.md:72), recruited via Round Tables, teachers and Facebook groups, plus 100 or more real Historian questions authored by someone other than the owner (Search Console queries, teachers, genealogists). Acceptance: dossier with dates linked from the method page; each scorecard row cites at least one non-author artifact.

gaps.area: Documentation / trust / Ask the Historian (citation permanence, link rot)
gaps.gap: Historian answers and unit cards will cite external hosts: Internet Archive page scans (reader_index deep links), LoC, NPS, HMDB, ABT (link-out tier). Link checking exists only for the guide PDF (docs-copy.md:635, lychee) and a weekly catalogue check (hist-eval.md:354); no report stores archived copies or alternate locators, and a grep finds no 'wayback' or 'perma.cc'. If a host moves or goes down, page-accurate citations, a headline A+ feature, rot silently.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'Citation permanence' (S-M). (1) Extend the source registry (sources.yaml, hist-sources-2-01) with locators[] holding at least 2 independent hosts per public-domain source (IA plus HathiTrust/Google Books/Wikisource/LoC where they exist) and an archive_url (Wayback Save Page Now) captured at ingest for every external URL cited on unit pages, Historian answers, /sources and the guide. (2) Because public-domain text is already ingested (raw cache about 75 MB), publish the extracted PD text of each cited page under /sources/text/<slug>/<page> (PD tier only, rights gate enforced) so quotes always resolve on our own host. (3) Nightly external-link checker (lychee) over /sources and cited URLs that opens an issue and switches the UI to archive_url after 3 failed checks. (4) Give dataset releases a DOI (Zenodo; seo-growth-26). Acceptance: no cited external URL without an archive_url; a simulated IA outage falls back in the UI; link check green.

gaps.area: Reliability / vendor risk (Mapbox cost, Netlify, PeerJS, Google, LLM)
gaps.gap: The plan concentrates on Netlify (hosting, RUM, Functions/Blobs, DNS), Mapbox (billed per map load, 50k free then USD 5 per 1,000 per infra-netlify.md:346; proprietary licence), a Google Maps key, the public PeerJS broker, Name.com, GitHub Actions and optionally an LLM API. Each report handles only its own vendor (infra-netlify-30 credits; bundle-anatomy-16 engine choice; pages-C-47 relay). No consolidated register defines numeric cost/terms triggers or tested exit paths. Traffic will change: about 3.4k map loads per month is the upper bound today (infra-netlify.md:1399) but the SEO programme, classrooms (30 per period) and bots can move it; infra-netlify.md:1399 marks billing alerts UNVERIFIED and no report confirms whether Mapbox offers a hard spend cap.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a 'Vendor register and exit triggers' (S). Table: vendor, dependency, lock-in, numeric trigger, exit path, tested yes/no. Examples: Mapbox trigger above 35k map loads per month or any price/ToS change leads to bundle-anatomy-16 option D/F (MapLibre plus PMTiles/NAIP) behind the 6-method map facade; Netlify alert at 70% of credits (hist-final-plan 9.4) plus the second-host snapshot from the backup item; PeerJS replaced by an owned relay or retired with Watch Together; Google key restricted plus click-to-load; LLM tier behind an env kill switch. Add a Mapbox cost circuit breaker: usage alerts at 50/70/90% of the free tier, check whether a spend cap exists (unverified), and the poster/tap facade so headless sessions (navigator.webdriver, known bot UAs) never initialise a map. Acceptance: register committed; a test alert fires; a headless run creates 0 map loads.

gaps.area: Mobile / in-app browsers and social referrals
gaps.gap: qa-ci.md:653 lists Facebook/Instagram/Reddit in-app browsers as 'none automated; spot check', although referrals from history groups and share cards make them a top entry point. In-app WebViews differ: storage may not persist into the default browser (layout choice, resume and bookmarks lost), no service worker/PWA install, Web Share, downloads and MediaRecorder often missing (Cinematic Export), sensor/camera permissions blocked (AR), and tighter WebGL memory. The chooser/persistence fixes do not address this.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add 'In-app browser mode' (S-M). Detect via UA tokens (FBAN/FBAV, Instagram, TikTok/musical_ly, Line, Reddit, GSA). (a) Make resume state URL-first (hash params) so a hand-off to Safari/Chrome keeps the view; (b) suppress install/notification prompts; (c) for features needing download, sensors, MediaRecorder or AR, show an 'Open in your browser' action (intent:// on Android, copy-link sheet on iOS) instead of failing; (d) default to the Lite boot (poster facade, reduced DPR) inside IABs; (e) add one physical iPhone and one Android IAB pass per release candidate to qa-ci T6, and Playwright UA emulation for feature gating. Acceptance: under an emulated IAB UA there are no console errors, export and AR pages show the hand-off message, and a deep link round-trips.

gaps.area: SEO / change management and baseline
gaps.gap: Several site-wide identity changes are scheduled close together: canonical form (seo-growth-03), product name (seo-growth-04), '/' split into landing plus '/map' (seo-growth-09), programmatic pages (seo-growth-13 onward) and the app cutover (prov-recon-39), while Search Console ownership has lapsed (seo-growth-01) so no baseline exists. With about 175 search referrals per 30 days (BRIEF T1) any ranking dip is unattributable if changes overlap, and rollback is impossible without a versioned redirect map.
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a sequencing rule to the roadmap (S). (1) Verify GSC and Bing via DNS TXT now and collect at least 28 days of baseline BEFORE the first canonical/URL change (performance, security and hygiene fixes need not wait). (2) Allow at most one identity-level SEO change per release train, in order: canonical form, then name, then the '/' split, then programmatic pages, at least 4 weeks apart, each with the redirect-matrix test (seo-growth Appendix D) and pre/post dashboards (impressions, clicks, indexed pages, CWV). (3) Keep a versioned redirect map for rollback and a no-touch window around the strangler cutover. (4) Annotate GSC/RUM/Analytics with release IDs. Acceptance: baseline export archived; the release calendar shows spacing; each SEO release has a stored before/after report.

gaps.area: Reliability / long sessions, projectors and kiosks
gaps.gap: No report tests long-running sessions (grep for 'soak' and 'kiosk' finds none), although classroom projectors, visitor-centre displays and the planned Present mode (ux-flows-13) keep the map running for hours. Known leak candidates exist today: the perpetual monuments rAF+setState loop (perf-runtime-02), up to 3 Mapbox instances, and a playback clock that jumps after backgrounding (app-latent-18).
gaps.recommended_plan_item: Add a nightly 60-minute soak job (S-M): Playwright/Chromium with CDP Performance.getMetrics and HeapProfiler on /map playing at 8x, looping days, opening/closing panels, switching layout and doing 20 bfcache back/forward cycles. Assert JS heap growth under 30 MB, DOM node count and listener count stable within plus or minus 5%, no long-task growth and stable p95 frame time. Request navigator.wakeLock only while playing and release it on pause/hidden; Present mode disables idle dimming. Acceptance: soak job green in CI; a unit test proves the wake lock is released on pause.
